Stack facts: Hono ^4.6 app on Cloudflare Workers (src/index.ts is the entry, export default app). TypeScript strict mode (pnpm typecheck = tsc --noEmit).
wrangler.jsonc already defines D1 binding named DB (database_name "dbms") and vars B2_ENDPOINT=https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com , B2_BUCKET=dbms-family-photos. .dev.vars has SESSION_SECRET.
Tests run with vitest. D1 is SQLite, so schema tests use better-sqlite3 (installed by another node). NEVER use Cloudflare KV anywhere.
DO NOT run any git commit - the lead commits. Stay strictly inside your write scope.
API CONTRACT (authoritative, do not redesign):
POST /api/signup {email,name,password,lang} -> 201 {user_id,email,name,lang}; 409 duplicate email.
POST /api/login {email,password} -> 200 {user} + Set-Cookie sid=...; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age=604800. Wrong password -> 401.
POST /api/logout -> 204 clearing cookie. GET /api/me -> 200 current user or 401.
GET /api/trees -> 200 {trees:[{tree_id,name,role}]}. POST /api/trees {name} -> 201 {tree_id,name}; creator row auto-inserted into tree_access.
POST /api/trees/:id/access {email,role} -> 201, creator-only; unknown email -> 404; invalid role -> 400.
GET /api/trees/:id/generations -> 200 {generations:[{gen,couples:[{couple_id,other_info,child_count,partners:[{person_id,name,gender,dob,dod},...]}}]} ordered by gen asc (any member role).
GET /api/persons/:id -> 200 full person record (members only). POST /api/trees/:id/persons -> 201 {person_id} (editor+). PUT /api/trees/:id/persons/:pid -> 200 (editor+, partial update, whitelisted fields). DELETE /api/trees/:id/persons/:pid -> 200 (editor+; also delete dependent child_of rows and null couple partner references).
POST /api/trees/:id/couples {partner_a?,partner_b?,other_info?} -> 201 {couple_id} (editor+). POST /api/trees/:id/couples/:cid/children {person fields} -> 201 {person_id} creating the person AND a child_of row (editor+).
DELETE /api/trees/:id -> 200 creator-only; cascades child_of, couple, person, tree_access, trees in that order.
GET /api/kinship?tree=:tid&from=:pid&to=:pid -> 200 {from,to,relation_key,path,gloss,terms:{en,hi,ta,bn}}; no relation found -> 404 {error:"no_relation"}. Members only.
POST /api/persons/:pid/photo multipart form field "file" -> 201 {photo_url} (editor+); when B2 creds missing -> 503 {error:"b2_not_configured"}.
Static assets: everything not under /api/* is served from web/ via the ASSETS binding.
Errors are JSON {error:string}. 401 unauthenticated, 403 wrong role, 404 missing resource. Role hierarchy viewer < editor < creator; trees.created_by counts as creator even without a tree_access row.
Auth internals: password hashing PBKDF2-SHA256, 100000 iterations, 16-byte random salt, stored as pbkdf2$100000$salt_hex$hash_hex (WebCrypto crypto.subtle). Session cookie: payload {"uid","exp"} JSON, base64url, plus "." + base64url(HMAC-SHA256(payload, env.SESSION_SECRET)). Stateless, no KV.
Consumed modules (read their sources for exact exported names before importing): src/kinship/index.ts exports classify(graph, fromId, toId) -> {relation_key, path} and TERMS + resolveTerms; graph input shape {persons, couples, child_of} loaded with three D1 queries over person/couple/child_of filtered by tree. src/storage/b2.ts exports uploadPhoto(env, key, body, contentType) and B2ConfigError; catch B2ConfigError -> respond 503 {error:"b2_not_configured"}. Photo object key format: <tree_id>/<person_id>/<random uuid>.jpg (or original extension).
Generations SQL (run via env.DB.prepare(...).bind(treeId).all()): WITH RECURSIVE bands AS (SELECT c.couple_id, c.tree_id, 1 AS gen FROM couple c WHERE c.tree_id = ?1 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM child_of co WHERE co.child_person_id = c.partner_a OR co.child_person_id = c.partner_b) UNION ALL SELECT kc.couple_id, b.tree_id, b.gen + 1 FROM bands b JOIN child_of co ON co.couple_id = b.couple_id JOIN couple kc ON kc.partner_a = co.child_person_id OR kc.partner_b = co.child_person_id) SELECT b.gen, c.couple_id, c.other_info, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM child_of co WHERE co.couple_id = c.couple_id) AS child_count, pa.person_id AS pa_id, pa.name AS pa_name, pa.gender AS pa_gender, pa.dob AS pa_dob, pa.dod AS pa_dod, pb.person_id AS pb_id, pb.name AS pb_name, pb.gender AS pb_gender, pb.dob AS pb_dob, pb.dod AS pb_dod FROM bands b JOIN couple c ON c.couple_id = b.couple_id LEFT JOIN person pa ON pa.person_id = c.partner_a LEFT JOIN person pb ON pb.person_id = c.partner_b ORDER BY b.gen. Group rows by gen into {gen, couples:[{couple_id, other_info, child_count, partners:[non-null partner objects]}]}.
TEST INFRASTRUCTURE: build a minimal D1-over-better-sqlite3 shim class (methods prepare(sql) returning {bind(...vals)} -> {all(), first(), run()}, plus exec(sql)) applying migrations/0001_init.sql contents via db.exec. Construct the Hono app with a factory (e.g. createApp(env)) so tests pass the shim as env.DB plus a test SESSION_SECRET. Drive requests with app.request(). Handle cookies by reading the Set-Cookie header from the login response and sending it back via the Cookie header. -- 0001_init.sql : initial D1 (SQLite) schema for dbms-family.
-- All timestamps are INTEGER unix epoch (seconds). dob/dod are ISO-8601 date
-- strings ('YYYY-MM-DD') so that lexicographic compare == chronological compare,
-- which the kinship engine uses to pick elder/younger (_el/_yo) terms.

CREATE TABLE users (
  user_id       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  email         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name          TEXT NOT NULL,
  password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  lang          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'en' CHECK (lang IN ('en','hi','ta','bn')),
  person_id     TEXT NULL REFERENCES person(person_id),
  created_at    INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE trees (
  tree_id    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name       TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_by TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(user_id),
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE person (
  person_id    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  tree_id      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES trees(tree_id),
  name         TEXT NOT NULL,
  gender       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (gender IN ('m','f','o')),
  dob          TEXT,
  dod          TEXT,
  height       TEXT,
  weight       TEXT,
  address      TEXT,
  mail         TEXT,
  phone        TEXT,
  job          TEXT,
  degree       TEXT,
  place        TEXT,
  other_info   TEXT,
  photo_url    TEXT,
  birth_order  INTEGER
);

CREATE TABLE couple (
  couple_id   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  tree_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES trees(tree_id),
  partner_a   TEXT REFERENCES person(person_id),
  partner_b   TEXT REFERENCES person(person_id),
  other_info  TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE child_of (
  couple_id       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES couple(couple_id),
  child_person_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES person(person_id),
  PRIMARY KEY (couple_id, child_person_id)
);

CREATE TABLE tree_access (
  tree_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES trees(tree_id),
  user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(user_id),
  role    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('creator','editor','viewer')),
  PRIMARY KEY (tree_id, user_id)
);

-- Static reference data: mirrors the TypeScript kin-term table for reporting.
CREATE TABLE kin_term (
  lang         TEXT NOT NULL,
  relation_key TEXT NOT NULL,
  term         TEXT NOT NULL,
  gloss        TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (lang, relation_key)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_person_tree ON person(tree_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_couple_tree ON couple(tree_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_child_child ON child_of(child_person_id);

import type { TermRow } from './types';

/** Flat rows mirroring migrations seed data (lang, relation_key, term, gloss). */
export const KIN_TERM_ROWS: Array<{ lang: 'en' | 'hi' | 'ta' | 'bn'; relation_key: string; term: string; gloss: string }> =
  (Object.keys(TERMS) as Array<keyof typeof TERMS>).flatMap(lang =>
    Object.entries(TERMS[lang]).map(([relation_key, row]) => ({ lang, relation_key, ...row })),
  );

export function resolveTerms(relationKey: string): {
  en: TermRow; hi: TermRow; ta: TermRow; bn: TermRow; gloss: string;
} {
  const pick = (lang: keyof typeof TERMS): TermRow =>
    TERMS[lang][relationKey] ?? { term: relationKey, gloss: '' };
  const en = pick('en');
  return { en, hi: pick('hi'), ta: pick('ta'), bn: pick('bn'), gloss: en.gloss };
}
